question: Around JPY 30,000/month, does one-provider concentration or multi-provider diversification create more usable work capacity for the current World SE workflow?

borrowed_semantics: next natural action instead of internal task list
human_attention only for a decision Human must make now
momo_pattern_reused.note: Adapted pattern only; this is not a MOMO/KIBI contract or canonical state.

fx_reference.note: Used only for approximate portfolio comparison; provider billing tax/localization can differ.

verified_plan_facts.capacity: 5x Plus usage; same Pro core capabilities as $200 tier
Pro+ has 3x Pro agent limit; Ultra has 20x Pro agent limit
Pro gives advanced-model research access; Max gives highest access and 10,000 Computer credits/month
4x free usage limit plus Gemini/Deep Research/Google integration

scenarios.strength: Maximum headroom inside one execution family; lowest switching overhead.
scenarios.weakness: One quota/failure domain and one provider worldview; the chosen provider must cover every major lane well.
scenarios.fit_for_current_world_se: Conditional: attractive only after one lane is proven to be the dominant bottleneck.

scenarios.strength: Maximum model/provider diversity, independent fallback lanes, broad research/coding/ecosystem coverage.
scenarios.weakness: High overlap and Human/tool switching cost; coding headroom remains only Cursor Pro while money is spent on several overlapping general/research assistants.
scenarios.fit_for_current_world_se: Better continuity than one-provider concentration, but likely over-diversified.

scenarios.strength: Same approximate spend as B, but concentrates capacity into the three observed lanes: upper reasoning/research, implementation, and Google ecosystem/second-model path.
scenarios.weakness: Less direct Claude/Perplexity access; cross-model review breadth is narrower unless accessed through Cursor or free/on-demand routes.
scenarios.fit_for_current_world_se: Best current structural fit before real monthly telemetry proves otherwise.

current: The original one-provider-vs-five-provider choice is probably the wrong abstraction. At nearly identical spend, a three-lane portfolio preserves provider diversity while putting more capacity into the currently observed bottlenecks and reducing Human switching cost.
risk: This is a structural allocation experiment based on verified entitlements plus current workflow evidence, not a month-long measured throughput benchmark. Actual value depends on task mix, model limits, taxes, and how often each lane saturates.
next: Use real limit events and completed-work evidence for one billing cycle. Upgrade only the lane that repeatedly blocks useful work; remove subscriptions that do not change outcomes.
human_attention: Do not buy five subscriptions merely to maximize coverage. If spending roughly JPY 30,000 now, test the three-lane allocation before jumping to a single $200 tier or a five-provider portfolio.
